title: Distribution Shape
learning_outcomes: Explain distribution shape and accurately refer to at least two syllabus subtopics.
Apply the main idea of distribution shape to a small example, trace, calculation, or scenario.
Identify one important assumption or failure mode and describe how to check it.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study distribution shape in the context of probability and statistics. You will connect the PDF subtopics to a small example and practice describing what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: Distribution Shape matters because it affects how data is collected, represented, analyzed, interpreted, or used in a decision. Check the task and assumptions before choosing a method.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: Statistics describes data and helps estimate what may be true beyond a sample. Every estimate should be accompanied by its assumptions, uncertainty, and practical context.

items.title: Symmetry and skewness
items.text: Define symmetry and skewness in relation to distribution shape; identify the input, output, assumptions, and who uses the result.

items.title: Kurtosis
items.text: Work through kurtosis using a small, synthetic example before scaling up. State what the calculation or method returns and why that result is useful.

items.title: Unimodal and multimodal distributions
items.text: Check the edge cases for unimodal and multimodal distributions: missing values, unusual ranges, different groups, time boundaries, or a changed input can affect the conclusion.

items.title: Outliers and distribution shape
items.text: Document the rule or choice for outliers and distribution shape so another learner can reproduce the analysis and understand its limitations.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: 1. Restate the question addressed by distribution shape. 2. Identify the input data, intended output, and assumptions. 3. Predict what the small example should show before reading its output. 4. Change one input or assumption, compare the result, and document what remains uncertain.

content_blocks.code:
import statistics
values = [2, 3, 3, 6, 10]
print("mean:", statistics.mean(values))
print("median:", statistics.median(values))

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the provided synthetic input, rerun or retrace the example, and change one value at a time. Do not use personal records, credentials, or data you are not authorized to access.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Keep the question, data grain, units, and assumptions explicit. If a result differs, inspect the input and steps in order. Avoid turning an observed association into a causal claim, treating a sample as the population, or assuming a small demonstration guarantees production behavior. Mean and median answer different questions and respond differently to skewed data.
